newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close with downward correction.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close with downward correction.

text.p: Argentina's bolsa snapped a winning streak Thursday and pulled back on profit-taking.
Traders said although stocks recovered some ground at the close they would remain soft as the week comes to an end.

"We took our cue from the U.S. Treasuries market today, which slumped while Wall Street recovered," said Emilio Alessandro of brokers Alessandro. "The reason is the bolsa had climbed and ignored Wall Street losses Wednesday, so today it simply got back in line with New York stocks."
The blue-chip MerVal index closed 0.8 percent lower at 686.04 against a high of 698.04 and a low of 682.75.
The MerVal, which is currently at a three-year high, still stands 1.7 percent higher on the week.

"We almost made it to the 700 mark today but cash flows ebbed, causing everyone to lock in profits," said one technical analyst. "I think we should pierce that level early next week with some more selling likely tomorrow."
Traders predicted bargain-hunters would start to eye stocks quoted strictly at home over the next few sessions.
"Many of the smaller blue chips have lagged ADRs in recent weeks and are good buys ahead of the corporate results period -- today Indupa and Acindar showed this," said Alessandro.
Petrochemical firm Indupa and steelmaker Acindar were the day's only MerVal gainers, up 3.2 percent 1.7 percent. Acindar was initiated by CS First Boston Thursday as a "hold."
Floor volume shrank to 25 million pesos from 31.8 million Wednesday, while over-the-counter turnover was fractionally lower at 129 million pesos.
The broad market index fell 0.9 percent, with losers outstripping winners 39 to 18 and 17 issues closing flat.
Heaviest main-tier losers were carmaker Sevel, pulp maker Celulosa and Banco de Galicia, off 2.6 percent, 2.5 percent and 2.4 percent, respectively.
Oil giant YPF erased strong early gains to close flat.
